text:
Maria: Ran the nightly canary perf-suite on canary-08 (10.0.8.14) ~22:30 UTC — saw a steady RSS climb during long-context generation. One worker eventually OOM'd. Suspect allocator fragmentation or KV cache not trimming. Can someone grab heapshots and allocator stats?

Alice: I can take this. Which PID / service?

Maria: PID 4123 (redwood-runtime), commit abc1234, model=v2-open, seq_len=4096 during repro. Crash seen in logs: oom-killer invoked.

Bob: Pinging for jemalloc stats — if this is jemalloc we should get stats_print and coredump. Quick commands:
```
sudo gdb -p 4123 -batch -ex 'thread apply all bt' -ex 'quit'
sudo gcore -o /tmp/core.4123 4123
curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | egrep 'rss|vm_rss'
echo 'stats_print' > /proc/$(pgrep -f redwood-runtime)/fd/1  # if jemalloc mallctl pipe available
```
If jemalloc isn't set up like that, run: MALLOC_CONF="stats_print:true" ./redwood-runtime (in a repro).

Carol: Also request heapshots (tcmalloc/heap-prof) if enabled. Frank, did we have tcmalloc on that build?

Frank: This binary uses jemalloc by default. We ship a non-instrumented build on canary -> no heap-profiles. We can still gcore + pmap to see RSS segments. I'll ssh and pull pmap -x output.

Erin: Quick check: canary-08 has large prefix/KV cache tuned to 6GB cap but per-shard caps are off at the moment (we forgot the rollout flag). That could explain growth if a single worker isn't trimming. Maria, did the workload include many repeated prefixes?

Maria: Yes — long-context streaming with many repeated prompts. KV cache lookups rising over time. Would like to confirm whether it's live allocation growth vs fragmentation.

Alice: I'll do an initial lightweight triage: pmap -x 4123, /proc/4123/smaps rollup, and get jemalloc epoch/stats using mallctl via a small C probe if needed. Pushing a tiny helper to run via nsenter.

Bob: If you can get /proc/4123/smaps_rollup that gives a quick RSS vs anon/dirty breakdown. Also run:
```
cat /proc/4123/limits
cat /proc/4123/smaps | egrep 'Private|Rss|AnonHugePages' | sort -u
```
And paste the top 30 lines.

Alice: On it. ETA 8–10m.

(infra-bot): Canary canary-08: automated perf test finished; avg latency +3% vs baseline, memory alert triggered (rss > 2GiB) — incidents.redwood/INC-2026 assigned to runtime-oncall.

Carol: I'll follow up with a quick bisect note — Maria, do you have the exact commit window when this started? We should check recent allocator-related commits (arena changes / defrag heuristics).

Maria: Regression started after deploy window 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC, range commit abc0000..abc1234. I suspect the allocator defrag heuristic change in abc05xx but not sure.

Frank: If it's defrag heuristics, we can temporarily revert that flag on canary to see if RSS still climbs. I can toggle runtime config for today's canary.

Erin: For repro, consider running the same long-context job locally with `--kv-cache=on --kv-cap=unbounded` to force growth. If local repro matches, we can run with jemalloc env to get stats.

Alice: Update: pmap -x shows many anonymous mappings, RSS ~2.3GB, VIRT ~6.1GB. /proc/4123/smaps_rollup:
- Size: 6161348 kB
- Rss: 2389120 kB
- Pss: 2375000 kB (approx)
Looks like a lot of anonymous heap. Uploading gcore now, will start jemalloc stats probe next.

Bob: Great. If gcore completes, run `llvm-symbolizer`/gdb on it and check top allocation sites in the backtrace. Also, get `jemalloc stats` output when you can.

Maria: Thanks team. If we confirm fragmentation, let's plan a short-lived rollback of the defrag tweak and run the same job for 3 cycles. Carol, can you prepare the rollback PR so infra can apply quickly?

Carol: Yep, I'll prep the PR and tag @Frank for deploy.

Alice: Uploaded core to /s3/canary/core.4123.tar.gz and pasted a trimmed backtrace gist: https://redwood-internal/gists/heap-backtrace-4123 (private). Jemalloc stats (partial):
"allocated: 1.9G
active: 2.1G
metadata: 24M
resident: 2.3G
"

Alice: Next steps: Frank toggle defrag flag on canary-08, re-run night job, watch RSS. If it stabilizes, we have cause. Otherwise, we dig deeper into KV cache eviction paths.

Frank: Toggling flag now (safe flip). Will report back in 20m.

Maria: Appreciate it. Assigning follow-ups: Alice (heapshots + core analysis), Bob (jemalloc deep stats + potential mallctl probe), Carol (rollback PR), Frank (apply toggle + monitor), Erin (repro on local). I'll open an incident doc and paste these findings. :thumbsup:

Alice: quick note — if anyone needs the gcore, ping me; it's big (~1.7GB).

Frank: Canary check after toggle: 20m in, RSS plateaued at ~1.1GB during the same workload. Looks promising.

Maria: Nice — hold on rollback PR until we confirm two successful cycles. If confirmed, we'll ship revert to staging + prod rollout plan.

Carol: PR opened: revert-defrag-heuristic-abc05xx, linked to incident. Tagging runtime-owners for review.

Bob: I'll continue jemalloc instrumentation to ensure no lingering leaks. Will post a short runbook afterwards for repro + collection commands.

Erin: Repro completed locally with defrag flag on = growth, off = stable. Confirmed.

Maria: Closing loop for now — great coordination. We'll run two more cycles overnight and decide morning. If anything changes, call @runtime-oncall.
